segments.beybladeDynamicsLock: Observable Beyblade dynamics lock: every active top is a rigid palm-sized gyroscope with one tip in continuous contact with the stadium after landing. High RPM produces rapid circumferential texture blur around the Attack Ring; center emblems may remain centered but perimeter markings may not stay crisp or frozen. The contact tip and center of mass define one coherent axis; the top never hovers. Any tilt produces continuous gyroscopic precession: the lean direction rotates around the contact point and may damp toward vertical at high RPM or widen as RPM falls, but it never freezes at one lean angle or compass direction. Tip friction, gravity, and the bowl tangent create a continuous curved trajectory with position continuous from frame to frame; tops do not hold a staged side-by-side formation, teleport, or pivot on a glued point. Each collision is a brief Attack-Ring-to-Attack-Ring impulse followed immediately by visible separation, tangential deflection or rebound, changed travel velocity, wobble, and some speed loss; tops never overlap, stick together, or cluster like magnets. Mechanical energy then decreases monotonically through friction and impacts: orbit speed and RPM decay, precession widens, the rim or base may scrape, and a fully stopped unsupported top falls onto its side. Preserve every owner's authored top design, axial spin direction, path, and outcome across cuts.
segments.rotationalCausalityLock: Rotational-causality lock: spin energy comes from the ripcord-driven launcher gear while the top is still mechanically engaged.
